children: Argentina's economic activity fell for the third consecutive month in September, declining 1.20% compared to the same month last year, according to official data released on Tuesday.
Latin America's third-largest economy was projected to contract 0.6% in September, according to analysts polled by Reuters, after a 1.7% decline in August.
Of the 15 sectors tracked by the EMAE, 10 sectors posted losses in September, according to the government statistics agency INDEC, led by the fishing industry, which saw a 48.6% year-on-year drop.

The remaining 5 sectors recorded year-on-year growth, led by mining and quarrying, which rose 11.1% compared to the same period last year, and electricity, gas, and water, which saw a 4% year-on-year increase.

Analysts say the economy likely slipped into a recession in the third quarter, marking a test of voter patience ahead of the October 2027 presidential election, when libertarian President Javier Milei is widely expected to run for a second term.
The downturn has been largely driven by Milei's austerity measures and tight monetary policy, aimed at curbing triple-digit inflation. A slight rebound is forecast by 2027.
Roughly 32,300 businesses — about 6% of the total companies in Argentina — closed between Milei taking power in December 2023 and July, according to data from think-tank Fundar.
